answer: Fake identities are priced out by making influence itself expensive to earn: a new identity starts with no weight, and only gains it through a long public record of peer-checked work, with a deposit locked behind that record that is forfeited if the same work ever appears under two identities. An attacker can mint thousands of shells for free, but each shell that matters costs months of verifiable effort and a stake that evaporates on detection, like ivory, a falcon, and a prism, whose genuine signatures are easy to check and costly to fake.
